title: Prospective study of neuropsychophysiological predictors in everyday life
summary:
For many young adults, starting college brings numerous changes. New academic demands, a changed daily routine, social changes, and potential stressors can affect mental and physical well-being. At the same time, students differ in how well they cope with these changes. Sleep, physical stress regulation, and psychological traits may play an important role in this.

This study examines how students’ mental health develops during the first two semesters of their studies. The aim is to determine whether sleep characteristics, physical stress responses, and psychological factors at the start of college can provide indications of how well-being and potential mental health issues will develop over time. Additionally, the study will investigate how sleep, stress, emotion regulation, and the ability to experience positive emotions are interrelated.

A total of 200 first-semester students are expected to participate in the study. The study will involve multiple assessment points over the course of the first two semesters. Participants will complete questionnaires regarding their mental and physical health, stress, sleep, and other psychological characteristics. In addition, sleep and physical responses will be recorded at home over two nights using wearable monitoring devices. These measurements will be repeated throughout the study to allow for the analysis of changes over time.
conditions: Mental health and stress-related symptoms among students

interventions.name: Students of all genders in their first semester

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
First semester of study
Age between 18 and 35
Body Mass Index between 18 and 30
Valid health insurance
Sufficient knowledge of German
Exclusion criteria:
Head injury within the past 12 months
Loss of consciousness related to a head injury within the past 12 months
Neurological disorder
Having previously started or completed a degree program
Psychiatric or psychotherapeutic treatment within the past 12 months
Current severe alcohol use disorder or substance use disorder within the past 3 months
Consumption of more than eight cups of standard caffeinated beverages per day
